title: Mistral publishes the weights of Large 4, Canada takes a stake of up to $1.6 billion in Cohere, Reddit says Google’s AI Mode does not send it traffic, OpenAI rewrites the rules it wants its models to follow, and a relay is turning the sandbox off on Codex and Claude Code.
summary: On 29 October 2026 Mistral released the weights of Mistral Large 4, the trillion-parameter model it had previewed on 6 October, at $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens. The same day Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E targeting up to CAD $7 billion, and the Prime Minister of Canada said the government will invest up to $1.6 billion in the company, in stages. On Reddit’s earnings call, Steve Huffman said AI Mode does not drive traffic, and that October search referrals fell by more than 1 million a week. OpenAI reorganised its Model Spec around five values and said current models do not yet fully reflect it. Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team reported an unauthorised relay that installs the real Codex and Claude Code tools and switches their sandbox off.
uncertainty: Large 4’s prices, the licence line and the scores named in the story are from Mistral’s weights post of 29 October. The preview post is dated 6 October. Hugging Face’s launch post the same day says the model is about 1 trillion parameters in total, about 49 billion active, with a 1 million token context. That post also reports different figures on tests Mistral names: Terminal-Bench 4 at 28.3% where Mistral says 41%, a Coding Agent Index of 49.8% where Mistral says 48%, 82% on the reproduce-and-patch slice of the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index where Mistral states a Cyber Index of 51%, and 93.3% attack resistance on Lakera’s B3 where Mistral says 97.1% against a 93.3% preview. The posts do not say the settings match. Cohere’s CAD $7 billion and CAD $35.7 billion are a target and the valuation that target would represent, not cash it says it has received. Canada’s $1.6 billion and $1.7 billion are the ceilings and the commitments on the Prime Minister’s release, to be made in stages. The 165% ARR growth and the 300 customers are Cohere’s. Reddit’s “more than 1 million” is not a precise count, and it is Reddit’s own search referrals. The relay account is Symantec’s, via Broadcom’s 29 October bulletin. It says there is no evidence of abuse so far.

stories.theme: Mistral published the weights of Large 4, a trillion-parameter model you can host, with a licence catch if you resell it
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026 Mistral released the weights of Mistral Large 4, which it calls Le Chonk. The preview had gone up on 6 October, with the weights promised by the end of the month. Mistral describes it as a 1-trillion-parameter model that takes text and images. Hugging Face’s launch post the same day says about 1 trillion parameters in total, about 49 billion active, and a context of 1 million tokens. On Mistral’s API, from 29 October, the price is $0.70 per million input tokens, $0.07 per million cached input tokens, and $2.10 per million output tokens. The weights are under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight licence, which Mistral calls a modified MIT licence: free to use, modify, fine-tune and commercialise, except that a business running a model-as-a-service has to take a separate commercial licence. Mistral says three more weeks of reinforcement learning put it first among open models on Cognition’s private FrontierCode 2.0, at 19.7%, and on Terminal-Bench 4.0, at 41%, up 13 percentage points from the preview, with 30% fewer output tokens. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index it reports 48%, tied with GLM-5.3, using 47% fewer tokens per task. It offers three reasoning modes, low, medium and high, and high is the default. On its cyber tests it reports 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index and an average refusal of 96.6% on malicious cyber requests, which it calls the highest it measures among open models, on the cyber prompts of JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm. It reports 73.3% on FinWorkBench, second among open models to Kimi K3, BrowseComp at 84.5% against 75% for an earlier checkpoint, and 97.1% attack resistance on the B3 benchmark against 93.3% in the preview. Hugging Face’s post the same day gives other readings of some of those tests: 28.3% on Terminal-Bench 4, a Coding Agent Index of 49.8%, 82% on the reproduce-and-patch part of the Cyber Index, and 93.3% on B3. The two posts do not say the settings were the same.
stories.matters: A model this size can now sit on hardware you control, at a posted API price you can put in a spreadsheet. The scoreboard that comes with it is the maker’s, and it does not match every figure published the same day.
stories.imply: Download it if you need to host the model. If you would sell access to other people, read the licence line before you do. Do not put a single percentage in a board slide until you have said whose test it is.
uses: Price a pilot at $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens, or run the weights yourself if the data cannot leave.
If the plan is to offer Large 4 as a service, get Mistral’s commercial licence first. Use inside your own company is the case the modified MIT allows.
Keep FrontierCode’s 19.7% and Terminal-Bench’s 41% labelled as Mistral’s. Note that Hugging Face published 28.3% for Terminal-Bench 4 the same day.
stories.example: A bank’s model team downloads the weights for a coding assistant that has to stay in its own network. It does not put 41% in the vendor note. It writes that Mistral reports 41% and Hugging Face reports 28.3%, and that legal still has to clear any plan to host the model for a client.
stories.audience: Teams choosing an open model they can run themselves, and anyone about to resell access to one.
stories.watch: Whether Mistral and Hugging Face say which settings produced the two Terminal-Bench numbers. The commercial-licence terms for a hosted service. Independent reruns of FrontierCode and the Cyber Index.

source.title: Mistral: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight, 29 October 2026
source.quote: The model is free to use, modify, fine-tune, and commercialize, with a single condition: businesses that operate a Model-as-a-Service offering must obtain a separate commercial license from Mistral before using the model commercially.

stories.theme: Canada will invest up to $1.6 billion in Cohere, and Cohere’s round is targeting up to CAD $7 billion
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026 Cohere said it had completed the initial close of a Series E targeting up to CAD $7 billion, which it said would represent a CAD $35.7 billion valuation. It called that the largest private financing round a Canadian technology company has undertaken. Schwarz Group is the lead. Cohere names Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital and the Government of Canada as new investors, and Inovia Capital, NVIDIA and Prosperity7 Ventures as returning ones. The same day the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, said the Government of Canada will make an equity investment of up to $1.6 billion, on commercial terms, in stages, with reporting against the commitments. In return Cohere will create at least 1,000 new Canadian technical jobs by 2030, commit at least $1.7 billion to additional computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030, keep its Canadian incorporation and headquarters, fund research partnerships, and keep working with the Canadian AI Safety Institute. Cohere said that since launching North, its agent platform, it ended the third quarter with 165% year-over-year growth in annual recurring revenue, and that over the past year its customer count rose 20-fold to 300. Named customers include Bell Canada, RBC, TD Bank, Fujitsu, PwC and Aston Martin Aramco. Cohere’s blog the same day says the round is meant to build frontier models, a platform customers can run themselves, and cyber defence, including a planned acquisition of AISLE.
stories.matters: A government is buying a share of a model company, and attaching jobs and a compute build to the stake. The headline number is a target, not a wire transfer.
stories.imply: If you buy from Cohere, your vendor now has a state on the cap table. If you cite CAD $7 billion, say “targeting up to”. If you cite $1.6 billion, say “up to”, and “in stages”.
uses: In a vendor note, separate three figures: Canada’s ceiling of $1.6 billion, Cohere’s target of up to CAD $7 billion, and the CAD $35.7 billion valuation Cohere says that target would represent.
Write down the conditions you can check later: 1,000 Canadian technical jobs and $1.7 billion of compute in Canada by 2030, headquarters staying in Canada.
Treat the 165% revenue growth and the 300 customers as Cohere’s account of its own year.
stories.example: A procurement lead adds a line to the Cohere file: the Canadian government is taking a staged stake of up to $1.6 billion, the company has promised 1,000 technical jobs and $1.7 billion of compute in Canada by 2030, and the CAD $7 billion round is a target at the initial close.
stories.audience: Finance and procurement teams who buy model access, and anyone reading a funding headline as cash in the bank.
stories.watch: How much of the CAD $7 billion is actually closed, and when. Whether Canada’s stake is reported against the jobs and the compute. What the AISLE combination changes for customers who wanted cyber work on their own machines.

source.title: Prime Minister of Canada: Canada announces landmark investment in Cohere, 29 October 2026
source.quote: Canada’s equity investment in Cohere will total up to approximately $1.6 billion and will be made in stages.

stories.theme: Reddit says Google’s AI Mode does not drive traffic, and October search referrals fell by more than 1 million a week
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026, on Reddit’s third-quarter earnings call, chief executive Steve Huffman said Google’s AI Mode does not drive traffic. The Verge reported the call. Huffman said: “Not for us, and not to anybody, as far as I know. That’s just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it’s not.” Reddit said search referrals in October dropped by more than 1 million a week on average. Huffman tied part of the loss to AI Mode and AI Overviews, which he said have evolved and, at a minimum, push everyone down the search page. He also said Reddit believes its machine-translated pages are ranking lower, which would fall mostly outside the United States. He said Reddit is still a top search term, that people still want Reddit, and that Google is crawling the site as hard as ever. Reddit said it will require people to log in, which Huffman said is better for the product, for ads, for safety rules, and for protecting Reddit’s data.
stories.matters: A site that lives on Google clicks is saying the new answer box does not send the visit. If your own pipeline starts the same way, October is the month to count.
stories.imply: Do not paste Reddit’s sentence onto your forecast. Count your own referrals. “More than 1 million a week” is Reddit’s figure, and it is not a precise count.
uses: Pull October referral traffic from Google and set it next to September before anyone rewrites the acquisition plan.
Separate AI Mode from the ordinary blue links. Huffman is talking about the answer box, not about every Google visit.
If a login wall is the proposed fix, say what it is for: ads, safety, and keeping the pages from being scraped. It does not put the Google click back.
stories.example: A publisher’s audience lead stops a slide that says “AI Mode will replace our Google traffic.” She adds October’s referral line, leaves the number as “down, and still being counted,” and asks search to split AI Mode from the rest.
stories.audience: Publishers, shops and marketers whose customers arrive from Google, and the finance partners who forecast that traffic.
stories.watch: Whether Reddit publishes a precise referral count rather than “more than 1 million.” Whether Google answers the claim. What happens to logged-out traffic once the login wall is up.

source.title: The Verge: Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode ‘does not drive traffic’, 29 October 2026
source.quote: The reality is, AI Mode does not drive traffic.

stories.theme: OpenAI rewrote its Model Spec around five values, and says today’s models do not fully follow it yet
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026 OpenAI updated the Model Spec, its public description of how it wants its models to behave. The revision organises the document around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimisation, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. OpenAI says faithfulness is the foundation: the model should understand what OpenAI, the developer and the user intend, not only follow an instruction word for word, and it should show assumptions so a person can correct them. A new section, “Consider context carefully,” says conversations, memories and other context should inform that reading in a way that respects privacy and the user’s control. OpenAI also added defaults on supporting human agency and on following relevant social norms, and expanded the guidance on side effects. It retired most of the detailed style rules. Style, it says, should follow what people prefer, while stronger defaults remain, including approaching questions objectively. The model should not take a side merely because it thinks that is what someone wants to hear. Throughout the Spec, the model is now called “GPT” rather than “the assistant.” OpenAI says it is exploring training methods so models learn why the principles matter. It also says the Spec is the behaviour it is working toward, and that current models do not yet fully reflect it.
stories.matters: The written rules for a widely used model just changed, including how memory and earlier chats should shape an answer. The company says the models have not caught up.
stories.imply: If your acceptable-use policy quotes an old style guide, it is quoting something OpenAI has mostly withdrawn. If someone says the model now “follows the new Spec,” ask them to read the sentence that says it does not yet.
uses: Replace any internal note that lists the old style rules. The five values are what OpenAI says it is aiming at.
Ask whoever runs your workspace what the model is allowed to remember, and how a person clears it. The new section is about that context.
Do not tell staff or customers that behaviour has already changed. OpenAI says the models do not fully reflect the Spec yet.
stories.example: A compliance lead updates the one-page note on ChatGPT. She deletes the line about a fixed tone, writes down the five values, and adds that OpenAI says current models do not yet fully follow the document.
stories.audience: People who write the rules for how staff may use ChatGPT, and anyone who has to explain a model’s behaviour to a customer.
stories.watch: When OpenAI says a named model actually reflects the new Spec. How “consider context carefully” shows up in memory controls an admin can switch. Whether developers can still override the defaults that are not safety boundaries.

source.title: OpenAI: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI, 29 October 2026
source.quote: The Model Spec describes the behavior we are working toward; our models do not yet fully reflect it.

stories.theme: A relay is installing the real Codex and Claude Code tools and switching their sandbox off
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026 Broadcom published a Symantec Threat Hunter bulletin: an unauthorised relay has been installing the genuine OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code command-line tools on company machines, then rewriting the configuration. The sandbox is switched off. On Codex, Symantec says, it is set to “danger-full-access.” Requests go to the relay’s servers instead of OpenAI’s or Anthropic’s. Symantec says this is not a flaw in the tools. They are doing what the changed settings tell them to do. Threat Hunter found the relay at a dozen organisations, in use since early 2026, mainly in mainland China, in markets where the vendors do not officially sell. There is no evidence the operator is abusing that position. The configuration, Symantec says, strips out the safeguards that are meant to contain the agent, and can expose an organisation whose staff use it.
stories.matters: The dangerous part is not a fake program. It is the real coding agent, with the box that limits it turned off, and with the prompts going somewhere else.
stories.imply: A normal-looking install is not enough. Check where the tool sends its requests, and whether the sandbox is still on. A dozen organisations is Symantec’s count, not a census.
uses: On machines that run Codex, look for a sandbox set to danger-full-access, and for a server address that is not OpenAI’s or Anthropic’s.
Treat a setup script that someone runs just after the official install as something to read first, especially if it came from a domain that only looks like the vendor.
If a machine used the relay, assume the prompts and files that passed through it could have been read. Symantec has not reported abuse. That is not the same as a clean machine.
stories.example: An IT lead searches the developer fleet for Codex configs pointing at an unfamiliar host. She finds two laptops, takes them off the network, and has the owners rotate every key those sessions could see.
stories.audience: Security and IT teams who allow Codex or Claude Code, and the developers who install them.
stories.watch: Whether OpenAI or Anthropic publish indicators of their own. Whether Symantec names the domains. How often the same pattern shows up outside the markets named in the bulletin.

source.title: Broadcom, reporting Symantec Threat Hunter: Sandbox flipped to danger-full-access, 29 October 2026
source.quote: This is not a vulnerability in Codex or Claude Code. The tools are behaving as designed once their configuration has been changed.

HF same day: about 1T / 49B active / 1M context; Terminal-Bench 4 28.3%; Coding Agent Index 49.8%; reproduce-and-patch 82%; B3 93.3%. Preview was 6 Oct.

Cohere and the Prime Minister, 29 Oct: initial close of a Series E targeting up to CAD $7 billion, which would represent CAD $35.7 billion; Schwarz leads; Canada will invest up to $1.6 billion in stages; at least 1,000 Canadian technical jobs and at least $1.7 billion of compute in Canada by 2030; Cohere says Q3 ARR up 165% year over year and customers up 20x to 300

The Verge, 29 Oct, Reddit earnings call: Huffman says AI Mode does not drive traffic; October search referrals down by more than 1 million a week on average; AI Overviews and AI Mode push results down the page; Reddit will require login

OpenAI 29 Oct: Model Spec reorganised around faithfulness to human intent, harm minimisation, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care; most style rules retired; model called GPT rather than the assistant; current models do not yet fully reflect the Spec

Symantec via Broadcom, 29 Oct: unauthorised relay installs genuine Codex and Claude Code, sets Codex sandbox to danger-full-access, routes traffic to its own servers; a dozen organisations since early 2026, mainly mainland China; not a vulnerability in the tools; no evidence of abuse so far
